neighbours.label: The particle or preposition that completes a fixed verb idiom whose meaning is not literal ('sell up', 'speak for' someone, Spanish 'dar por'), not the same preposition in its literal use after an ordinary verb (waited for, written by, arrived from).
fire: After the harvest failed again, the brothers decided to sell up and move to the city.
The baker sold up his shop last spring and retired to Cornwall.
I think I can speak for everyone here when I thank our host.
The new spokesman will speak for the company at tomorrow's hearing.
En la reunión, la alcaldesa dio por terminada la discusión.
Los jueces dieron por válido el gol a pesar de las protestas.
Nadie puede dar por hecho que el contrato se firmará mañana.
As the eldest daughter, she often spoke for her younger siblings at meetings.
quiet: After the harvest failed again, the brothers waited for news from the city.
The baker opened up his shop at six and baked bread for the village.
I think everyone here is grateful for the food our host prepared.
The new spokesman arrived from the head office for tomorrow's hearing.
En la reunión, la alcaldesa habló de la discusión con los vecinos.
Los jueces miraron por la ventana mientras el público protestaba.
Nadie puede salir por la puerta antes de que se firme el contrato.
As the eldest daughter, she often cooked for her younger siblings at night.
